Net benefit across treatment thresholds

Source: R/decision_curve.R
mm_decision_curve.Rd

Decision curve analysis. For each threshold probability the function reports the net benefit of treating by the model, of treating everybody, and of treating nobody, so the three can be read against each other.

Usage

mm_decision_curve(
  obs,
  pred,
  thresholds = seq(0, 0.5, by = 0.01),
  positive = NULL
)

Arguments

obs

The observed outcome. Any column mm_model() accepts: 0/1, logical, or a two-level factor or character vector.

pred

Predicted probabilities, for instance the .pred column of mm_predict().

thresholds

Threshold probabilities, in [0, 1).

positive

The level that means the event, passed to the same rule mm_model() uses. NULL infers it, and warns when it has to.

Value

A data frame with one row per threshold: threshold, net_benefit_model, net_benefit_all, net_benefit_none, and the n, n_dropped and prevalence the curve was computed on.

Details

A threshold is the probability at which a reader would opt for the action. It carries the exchange rate between the two mistakes: at a threshold of 0.1 a reader is saying one missed event costs about nine unnecessary treatments, and the weight t / (1 - t) on false positives below is that statement written as arithmetic.

The curve says which strategy has the highest net benefit over the range of thresholds a reader might hold. It does not say the model is calibrated, and it is not a substitute for mm_validate(): a model can win on net benefit over a narrow band of thresholds and still be systematically wrong about the level, which is what a calibration intercept measures and what mm_recal_intercept() corrects.

Computing a decision curve is not the same as being entitled to publish one. Net benefit is an explicit trade of a benefit against a harm, so the curve means nothing until the decision-maker, the action and the two outcomes being traded are named. This function supplies the arithmetic and takes no view on whether that has been done.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 11)
project <- mm_project("dca", "event", c("age", "bmi"),
                      positive_class = 1, cohort = cohort)
fit <- suppressWarnings(mm_model(project, cohort))
scored <- mm_predict(fit, cohort)
curve <- mm_decision_curve(cohort$event, scored$.pred,
                           thresholds = seq(0, 0.3, by = 0.05),
                           positive = 1)
curve[, c("threshold", "net_benefit_model", "net_benefit_all")]
#>   threshold net_benefit_model net_benefit_all
#> 1      0.00       0.096666667     0.096666667
#> 2      0.05       0.049473684     0.049122807
#> 3      0.10       0.009259259    -0.003703704
#> 4      0.15       0.012352941    -0.062745098
#> 5      0.20       0.001666667    -0.129166667
#> 6      0.25      -0.003333333    -0.204444444
#> 7      0.30      -0.001428571    -0.290476190
